guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our lean toward Ole Miss starts with the passing game. Through three games, Trinidad Chambliss had thrown for 924 yards and seven touchdowns, while Ole Miss was averaging an SEC-best 330.7 passing yards and operating at one of the fastest tempos in the country. That profile matters against a Missouri defense that returned only two listed starters and lost 10 from last season’s group. We see more potential for Ole Miss to create separation through sustained passing volume than the market appears to be pricing.

The counterargument is Missouri’s rushing game. Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game last season, while Ole Miss allowed 159.0 per game through its first three contests. Our matchup numbers also identify the ground game as Missouri’s clearest offensive opening, even though they are less favorable toward its passing efficiency. At the same time, we rate Ole Miss more favorably at preventing scoring opportunities than its raw yardage totals suggest.

For us, those competing signals explain the pass. Our overall numbers prefer Ole Miss, but Missouri has a credible way to shorten the game and limit margin through the run. The market is close enough to our expectation that the available price does not leave enough room for that matchup risk.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Missouri’s rushing offense against the Ole Miss front. Missouri’s longer-run production on the ground is the clearest challenge to our Ole Miss lean, especially given what Ole Miss allowed early in the season. If Missouri consistently stays ahead of the chains, creating the separation our model anticipates becomes more difficult.

If Ole Miss limits those early-down gains and pushes Missouri toward its less efficient passing profile, the matchup shifts back toward the home side. That is the football tension most likely to determine whether Ole Miss can turn an advantage into margin.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Sept. 3.
Missouri produced 562 total yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, including 357 passing and 205 rushing, while converting 6-of-10 third downs and both fourth-down attempts.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime after outgaining the Golden Lions 376-6 in the first half.
Missouri's defense held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 total yards, 13 first downs and a 3-of-13 third-down conversion rate.
Missouri forced five three-and-outs against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

opponent_notes.fact: Missouri is scheduled to play at Ole Miss on Oct. 17, 2026; the guide lists Ole Miss at No. 9 in the AP poll and No. 10 in the Coaches Poll.
Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. transferred from Ole Miss.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons is listed as Missouri's starting quarterback, with sophomore Matt Zollers as the backup.
In his Missouri debut, Simmons completed 17-of-19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Simmons' 89.5% completion rate and 270.4 passer rating were the highest by a quarterback in a Missouri debut.
Simmons was Ole Miss' opening-game starter in 2025 and later completed 4-of-5 passes for 64 yards in the CFP First Round against Tulane.
Backup quarterback Matt Zollers completed 8-of-12 passes for 87 yards and scored his first collegiate rushing touchdown in the 2026 opener.

Missouri returned five offensive starters from 2025: Green, Giudice, running back Ahmad Hardy, tight end Brett Norfleet and Peagler.
Missouri lost 2025 starting quarterback Beau Pribula, center Connor Tollison, tackle Keagen Trost and starting receivers Kevin Coleman Jr., Marquis Johnson and Joshua Manning.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee is listed as Missouri's starting H receiver; he started all 15 games for Ole Miss in 2025 and 12 games in 2024.
Lee recorded five catches for 89 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown, in his Missouri debut.
Donovan Olugbode established career highs of seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns in the season opener.
Running back Jamal Roberts is listed as the starter and rushed 13 times for 47 yards and a touchdown in the opener.
Roberts surpassed 1,000 career rushing yards in the opener after setting 2025 career highs with 124 carries, 753 yards and six rushing touchdowns.
Left tackle Cayden Green allowed two sacks, two quarterback hits and three hurries over 750 snaps in 2025, according to PFF.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned two listed defensive starters from 2025 and lost 10, including defensive linemen Chris McClellan and Zion Young, linebacker Josiah Trotter and cornerback Toriano Pride Jr.
Ole Miss transfer Chris Graves Jr. is listed as a starting Missouri cornerback after appearing in 41 games over three seasons for the Rebels and starting nine games in 2025.
Auburn transfer Robert Woodyard Jr. is listed as Missouri's starting middle linebacker after making 11 starts and recording 67 tackles in 2025.
